claims.title: First settlement of Finland
claims.summary: People moved into Finland as the Ice Age glaciers retreated, settling along the coasts and waterways; the land was later inhabited by Finnic-speaking peoples and, in the north, the Sami.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-8800bce-first-settlement-of-finland, claim TL:FIN:event:8800bce:first-settlement-of-finland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Turku and the Christianization of Finland
claims.summary: Carried by the Swedish crusades, Latin Christianity spread through Finland; Turku (Abo), founded in the thirteenth century, became the principal town and episcopal seat of the eastern realm.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1249-turku-and-the-christianization-of-finland, claim TL:FIN:event:1249:turku-and-the-christianization-of-finland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Noteborg
claims.summary: The peace of Noteborg fixed an approximate frontier between the Swedish and Russian spheres in Karelia, assigning Finland to Sweden's orbit and splitting the Karelians between Catholic west and Orthodox east.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1323-treaty-of-noteborg, claim TL:FIN:event:1323:treaty-of-noteborg, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mikael Agricola and written Finnish
claims.summary: The Reformation-era bishop Mikael Agricola created written Finnish, translating the New Testament in 1548 and laying the foundation of Finnish literary culture.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1548-mikael-agricola-and-written-finnish, claim TL:FIN:event:1548:mikael-agricola-and-written-finnish, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Finnish War and the end of Swedish rule
claims.summary: Russia conquered Finland from Sweden in the war of 1808-09, ending some six centuries during which Finland had formed the eastern half of the Kingdom of Sweden.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1808-the-finnish-war-and-the-end-of-swedish-rule, claim TL:FIN:event:1808:the-finnish-war-and-the-end-of-swedish-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Finland becomes an autonomous Grand Duchy
claims.summary: By the Treaty of Fredrikshamn Sweden ceded Finland to Russia; it became the autonomous Grand Duchy of Finland, joined to the empire through the tsar, who reigned as Grand Duke, and kept its own laws and religion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1809-finland-becomes-an-autonomous-grand-duchy, claim TL:FIN:event:1809:finland-becomes-an-autonomous-grand-duchy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Helsinki made the capital
claims.summary: The capital was moved from Turku to Helsinki, nearer to Saint Petersburg, and the town was rebuilt as a neoclassical capital of the Grand Duchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1812-helsinki-made-the-capital, claim TL:FIN:event:1812:helsinki-made-the-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Elias Lonnrot publishes the Kalevala
claims.summary: Lonnrot published the Kalevala, a national epic assembled from oral folk poetry collected in Karelia; it strengthened the Finnish language and fed the national awakening that would culminate in independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1835-elias-lonnrot-publishes-the-kalevala, claim TL:FIN:event:1835:elias-lonnrot-publishes-the-kalevala, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Russification and Finlandia
claims.summary: Nicholas II's February Manifesto curtailed Finnish autonomy, beginning a campaign of Russification; resistance found voice in Jean Sibelius's tone poem Finlandia, composed that same year.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1899-russification-and-finlandia, claim TL:FIN:event:1899:russification-and-finlandia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A modern parliament and votes for women
claims.summary: Finland adopted a unicameral parliament elected by universal suffrage, becoming the first country in Europe to grant women the right to vote and to stand for election.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1906-a-modern-parliament-and-votes-for-women, claim TL:FIN:event:1906:a-modern-parliament-and-votes-for-women, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Declaration of independence
claims.summary: The Parliament of Finland approved a declaration of independence amid the turmoil of the Russian Revolution, ending more than a century as an autonomous Grand Duchy of the Russian Empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1917-declaration-of-independence, claim TL:FIN:event:1917:declaration-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Soviet Russia recognises Finland
claims.summary: Lenin's Bolshevik government formally recognised Finnish independence on the last day of 1917, calculating that it could not retain the periphery of the former empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1917-soviet-russia-recognises-finland, claim TL:FIN:event:1917:soviet-russia-recognises-finland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Finnish Civil War
claims.summary: From late January to 15 May 1918 Finland was convulsed by civil war between socialist Reds and conservative Whites under Mannerheim; the Whites won, but some 36,600 died, many in executions and prison camps.

sources.label: How Finland found a road to reconciliation after the Civil War of 1918

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1918-the-finnish-civil-war, claim TL:FIN:event:1918:the-finnish-civil-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Republican constitution
claims.summary: Finland adopted a republican constitution in 1919, establishing a parliamentary republic with a strong presidency rather than the monarchy that conservatives had briefly favoured after the civil war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1919-republican-constitution, claim TL:FIN:event:1919:republican-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Aland Autonomy Act
claims.summary: Finland granted the Swedish-speaking Aland Islands wide-ranging cultural and political autonomy, anticipating the conditions the League of Nations would attach to its sovereignty the following year.

sources.label: The special status of the Aland Islands
sources.publisher: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland

sources.label: The Aland example: Autonomy protects a minority

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1920-aland-autonomy-act, claim TL:FIN:event:1920:aland-autonomy-act, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: League of Nations awards Aland to Finland
claims.summary: The Council of the League of Nations awarded sovereignty over the Aland Islands to Finland, while obliging it to guarantee the islanders' Swedish language, culture and self-government, a landmark of peaceful conflict resolution.

sources.label: The special status of the Aland Islands
sources.publisher: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland

The Aland Islands Solution: a precedent for successful international disputes settlement

claims.title: Convention on the demilitarisation of Aland
claims.summary: An international convention confirmed the demilitarisation of Aland dating from the 1856 Treaty of Paris and added its neutralisation, keeping the islands outside any theatre of war.

sources.label: The Legal Basis of Aland's Demilitarization and Neutralization
The special status of the Aland Islands
sources.publisher: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland

claims.title: The far-right coup attempt fails
claims.summary: An attempted uprising by the extreme-right Lapua movement collapsed within days when the majority of Finns rejected it, and the parliamentary republic held firm through the interwar years.

sources.label: How Finland found a road to reconciliation after the Civil War of 1918

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1932-the-far-right-coup-attempt-fails, claim TL:FIN:event:1932:the-far-right-coup-attempt-fails, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Winter War begins
claims.summary: The Soviet Union invaded Finland on 30 November 1939 after Finland refused to cede territory near Leningrad; the outnumbered Finns mounted a celebrated defence through the winter of 1939-40.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1939-the-winter-war-begins, claim TL:FIN:event:1939:the-winter-war-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Moscow Peace Treaty cedes Karelia
claims.summary: The Winter War ended in March 1940 with Finland keeping its independence but ceding much of Karelia, including Viipuri; the inhabitants of the lost lands were evacuated into the rest of Finland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1940-moscow-peace-treaty-cedes-karelia, claim TL:FIN:event:1940:moscow-peace-treaty-cedes-karelia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Continuation War
claims.summary: Allied with Germany after its 1941 invasion of the USSR, Finland fought the Continuation War to recover Karelia, but a Soviet offensive in 1944 forced it to seek an armistice.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1941-the-continuation-war, claim TL:FIN:event:1941:the-continuation-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Moscow Armistice and cession of Petsamo
claims.summary: The Moscow Armistice ended the Continuation War, restoring the 1940 border, returning Petsamo to the Soviet Union, leasing Porkkala as a naval base, and imposing reparations.

sources.label: Draft Peace Treaty with Finland (Paris Peace Treaty terms)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian (FRUS)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1944-moscow-armistice-and-cession-of-petsamo, claim TL:FIN:event:1944:moscow-armistice-and-cession-of-petsamo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Paris Peace Treaty and the Karelian evacuees
claims.summary: The 1947 Paris Peace Treaty confirmed the cession of Karelia and Petsamo and reparations of 300 million dollars; some 400,000 Karelian evacuees were resettled within Finland's new borders.

sources.label: Draft Peace Treaty with Finland (Paris Peace Treaty terms)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian (FRUS)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1947-paris-peace-treaty-and-the-karelian-evacuees, claim TL:FIN:event:1947:paris-peace-treaty-and-the-karelian-evacuees, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty with the Soviet Union and neutrality
claims.summary: A 1948 treaty of friendship with the Soviet Union framed Finland's Cold War policy of strict neutrality and non-alignment, later known as 'Finlandization', under which it preserved its democracy and independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1948-treaty-with-the-soviet-union-and-neutrality, claim TL:FIN:event:1948:treaty-with-the-soviet-union-and-neutrality, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Helsinki Final Act
claims.summary: Under President Kekkonen, neutral Finland hosted the Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe, whose Helsinki Final Act of 1975 became a landmark of Cold War detente.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1975-the-helsinki-final-act, claim TL:FIN:event:1975:the-helsinki-final-act, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Finland joins the European Union
claims.summary: After a 1994 referendum in which about 57 per cent voted yes, Finland joined the European Union on 1 January 1995 with Sweden and Austria, and later adopted the euro.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-1995-finland-joins-the-european-union, claim TL:FIN:event:1995:finland-joins-the-european-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Finland applies to join NATO
claims.summary: Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 reversed Finnish opinion on military alignment; together with Sweden, Finland applied to join NATO, abandoning its long-standing non-alignment.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-2022-finland-applies-to-join-nato, claim TL:FIN:event:2022:finland-applies-to-join-nato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Finland becomes NATO's 31st member
claims.summary: Finland deposited its instrument of accession and joined NATO as its 31st member on 4 April 2023, ending generations of neutrality and more than doubling the Alliance's land border with Russia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Finland: Six centuries with Sweden, a century with Russia, and a hard-won independence between two great powers.", terralore.co/country/FIN/chronicle#ev-2023-finland-becomes-nato-s-31st-member, claim TL:FIN:event:2023:finland-becomes-nato-s-31st-member, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
